teaching: The book is titled Kunooz al-Hikmah al-madhkurah li-arbab al-ismah, meaning Stored Treasures of Wisdom for the Masters of Infallibility.
The Aimmah Tahirin possess kulli ismah (total infallibility), making sin and error impossible for them.
The duat, especially the qaimi duat, possess only juzi ismah (partial infallibility), and for them the treasures of wisdom were stored.
The distinction between kulli and juzi ismah was clarified in a risalah by Sayyidna Ali bin Hussain al-Jamari.
The book was written by Sayyidna Ali bin Hibatullah, called al-Shamsi, son of Sayyidna Hibatullah bin Ibrahim.
Sayyidna Ali bin Hibatullah died during his father's lifetime, becoming a ghayr-munfarid Dai (non-independent Dai).
Sayyidna Ismail bin Hibatullah was tenth in the order of succession and had the most excellent form among the wulat.
Sayyidna Jafar bin Hibatullah, the 74th Dai's brother, composed qasidahs including the opening of al-Kawakib al-Durriyah.
Above the Bismillah is written the Ism al-Azam (Greatest Name), whose nur is more excellent than the nur of the Bismillah.
Sayyidna Abd al-Ali bin Hasan al-Wajih wrote a risalah proving the nur of the Ism al-Azam is greater than that of the Bismillah.
In the Teseri script, the first dot above the Ism al-Azam is a khatam (seal/ring) alluding to the Ahl al-Sharif.
The madd (elongation mark) above the Ism al-Azam refers to the assistance received from the Hudud Aliyah.
There are three types of nasut: nasut adna (lowest), nasut awsat (middle), and nasut khas (special).
The lowest nasut is also called nasut tabii (natural) or nasut tanasuli (procreative); next is nasut dhilli (shadow); highest is nasut khas (special).
The nasut khas is made from the riyadh (gardens) of the ahl al-ikhtisas, who are the hudud al-dawah, muminin, and hudud of the hadarat.
The first existent thing (awwal mawjud) is the First Intellect (aql-e-awwal); the last is the believer who enters the dairah-e-iman.
The First Intellect and the last existent thing (the believer) are equal in their inability to comprehend God's exalted essence.
The Quranic word shay (thing) in verses like inna Allaha ala kulli shayin qadir refers specifically to the believer.
Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman stood up to receive believers, saying the believer is his companion in the Ahl al-Sharif.
Sayyidna Hussain bin Ismail wrote that Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Muhammad is afdal al-mawjudat (most excellent of existing things) among the believers of the dawah.
The Prophet's Miraj ascent occurred through the special nasut formed from the riyadh of the ahl al-ikhtisas.
Jabarut means the powerful one, derived from jabr.
After his Ghadir Khumm declaration, the Prophet lived his remaining life in the hijab of Ali, and Ali lived in the hijab of the Prophet.
Sayyidna Ismail bin Ibrahim stated that the awsiya pass away before the natiq (speaker-prophet).
The Prophet declared Ali was from him as flesh-of-flesh and blood-of-blood, from a single soul (ruh wahidah).
The Prophet gave Ali the right to divorce Aisha after his passing, an authority confirmed by the Mubahalah verse (anfusana wa anfusakum).
The al-ashir (Tenth) was veiled by the Prophet, referring to the juz-e-idafiyyah (relative part) of this qawr's sahib al-qawr.
Lady Fatimah is the khalifatu abiha and hujjatu baliha and the greatest hujjah (hujjat al-uzma).
Lady Fatimah is alluded to by the first night of Shahr al-Rajab al-Murajjab, attributed to Ali.
Umar testified on the minbar that the minbar belonged to Hasan/Hussain's father, conceding their high rank.
Lady Fatimah al-Zahra was the appointed successor over the Muhammadan community; the Prophet would stand and seat her in his place.
Hasan is the mustawda (trustee) of the secret of Imamate; all the duat are connected to Imam Hasan.
The Aimmah are connected to Sayyidna Hussain.
Surah al-Nas alludes to Sayyidna Hasan, with nas referring to those who are manusina bid-dawah.
Rabb al-falaq points to where the Imamate began through splitting (falaq).
Hussain made his own occultation manifest through being killed by the people of doubt; his real self was protected.
Asrar (secrets) refer to intentions (niyyat); anwar (lights) refer to the suwarat (luminous forms) of the duat.
Sayyidna Sulayman is jami al-asrar (assembler of secrets) of the duat of Yemen who came after Sayyidna Dhuayb bin Musa.
All Aimmah until Resurrection are veiled by Amir al-Muminin; they are his hijab and he is their veiled essence.
This dawr lasts fifty thousand years, included within the dawr of the Qaim; the seven dawr al-satr eras ended with Sayyidna Sulayman.
Jafar the seventh refers to the 28th Dai (Sayyidna Jafar) who is seventh in the protected secret.
Mim refers to Muhammad bin Fuad, the non-independent intermediate Dai who established jihad among the people.
Ayn refers to Sayyidna Ali bin Sulayman; from his tongue gushed the springs of secrets of doctrines.
Shual al-Anwar is the first book in the realities (haqaiq) and subtleties (daqaiq); Sayyidna Jafar wrote only on hujjat and tawil, never on haqaiq.
Muhammad bin Ismail was the first Dai to emigrate from Yemen to Najran and the first/only Dai granted permission to lead prayers in ghayr jazirah (outside Arabia), having led prayers in Habasha.
Sayyidna Rashid bin Isa, after becoming Dai, stood in his prayer niche for six years performing missed prayers.
The Quranic command to seek refuge (taawwudh) before reciting the Quran is because misinterpretation by daiyya has led communities astray.
Taawwudh should not be done during the adhan; only Bismillah is said.
In the adhan, the last La ilaha illallah is recited softly, alluding to the last mushir who departs in the blink of an eye.
In the dais lifetime, asrar means riyah; anwar means surah; the riyah emerge for three days after burial.
Hawzah is a place around which a wall is drawn, here meaning the center of the dawah.
For every dai there is a Firaun (Pharaoh) opposing him; the principle li-kulli dain firawn applies in every era.
The tasbih of the Pir is Ya Rahim Ya Rahman; though in the Quran Rahman always precedes Rahim, books may invert for rhyme.
In Surah al-Hajj verses 58-65 are eight blessed verses called Mafatih al-Jinan, keys to the eight heavens.
One verse in Surah al-Hajj contains fifteen of the Asma al-Husna in a single sentence.
Ya Aliyyu Ya Azim is the tasbih recited on Wednesdays.
Hadrat al-samiyah refers to the dai; Alamuddin is one of Sayyidna Hibatullah's titles.
The dai's sins (aswa) are actually missed good deeds intended but not accomplished due to obstacles.
The Quranic ma taqaddama min dhanbika wa ma taakhkhara refers not to the Prophet's own being (which is pure) but to his hujab who rise from the hudud al-dawah.
One Prophetic sin alluded to was an inclination by the Prophet's hujab toward Abu Bakr, wanting a portion of Ali's wilayah given to him.
The verse Wa in ashrakta layahbatanna amaluka warns that including anyone in Ali's wilayah nullifies one's work.
Naqid is one who can decide good or bad; basir is the one with insight; one has authority of taqdim and taakhir over hudud.
The questioner cannot directly drink from the spring's source (the Dai) so requests the book in writing.
Alam al-Ibda was created not from a thing (la min shayin) and not in a thing (wa-la fi shayin); inquiring about its modality is forbidden.
Speculating about how the ibda emanated is misguidance and shirk, plunging one into the sea of destruction.
Alam al-Ibda is identical with the Intellects themselves (alam al-ibda hum al-uqul); the Intellects are not separate from the world.
The Imam has three hijabs in broad count: tabii, dhilli, and khas, then the dhat-i Imam.
In the tasbih, Allahu Akbar points to hijab al-adna (tabii), Subhanallah to hijab al-khas, and the third part to dhat-i Imam.
The nasut khas is built in the Bayt al-Haram, not bound by loins, wombs, courtyards, houses, or graves.
Death, killing, and passing-away occur to the lowest of the veils (adna al-hujub), not to the real self of the Imam.
With Imam Hussain, what was killed at Karbala was a hijab; the real self was protected.
For Rasulullah, the ghusl veil was Abdullah ibn Masud; the buried veil was Abdullah ibn Rawahah; the ziyarat veil is Ubayy ibn Kab.
Ubayy ibn Kab is the Prophet's ummi al-ruhaniyyah (spiritual mother) and his first teacher who taught the laws of Adam.
Janab-i Khadijah was the final pre-bathah teacher of the Prophet and became teacher of Janab-i Ali.
Ibn Maryam refers to Ali, with Maryam being Khadijah; for this reason Maryam was exempted from the five prayers.
Before the existence of heaven and earth there were dhawat al-nadimah (penitent essences) divided into fifteen categories; from the first the celestial spheres were made.
Fudlah (remnant) is only what remains of a body after the spirit and soul emanate.
The jussa ibdaiyyah takes vicegerency of the Ashir (Tenth Intellect) in a partial capacity; the kulli vicegerency belongs to the akhir mawr.
Believers are in the fifteenth category of the nadimin and in its tenth division; each category has ten divisions.
The Ashir was originally the third intellect; through wahm al-musawat (illusion of equality) he claimed parity with Mumbaith al-Awwal and fell.
No two persons can sit at the same rank; even two Imams (Hasan and Hussain) or two duat had differing ranks.
Mumbaiths gaze was on the surah ilmiyyah (intellectual form) of the First Intellect; Ashir's gaze was on the surah amaliyyah (practical form).
Shirk is the only sin Allah will not forgive; until disbelievers accept Islam they cannot ascend.
Uyafa are non-Muslims or Muslims who love Ahl al-Bayt and abide by shariah; they gradually ascend into iman.
Al-aziz al-alim refers to the Ashir, who knows how many mawrs are needed for purification of each troop.
Falak al-mustaqim is the encompassing sphere (falak al-muhit), the highest sphere, invisible, beyond which the alam al-ruhani begins.
The light of the sun derives from the light of falak al-mustaqim; at end-of-kawr, falak al-mustaqim ascends in place into the tenth arsh and becomes an intellect qaiman bil-fil.
When the believer dies, his surah goes to the hudud-e uliyyah; his riyat go into the aflak (sun, Jupiter); his fuzala ascend through the mihrab and to the center of his jazirah.
The believer's fuzala while ascending are called zuubat, then become zakhair (treasures).
The four pillars of the Bayt are the asatir; they are the atqiyah (pious ones) in physical form.
At the Imam's passing, he dissolves in the qalb (Baytullah) and becomes substance and strength for the hearts of the learned hudud of the dawah.
The Quranic burhan rabbihi seen by Yusuf was this mawad obtained from the Imam.
At the hudud's passing, the mawad given them in life returns to its origin in the qalb.
The next Imam's soul is formed from what is supplied from the qalb, the water around it, and the bataih adjacent.
Sayyidna Hibatullah bin Ibrahim clarified this matter in his treatise Saqilat al-Quloob, also called al-Munawwirah lil-Basair and al-Musfiyah lil-Suwar.
In the Imam are nasut and lahut, paralleling the negation and affirmation of the shahadah.
The Quranic kullu shayin ahsaynahu fi imamim mubeen uses ahsayna (enumerated, retaining individuality), not jamana (gathered/jumbled).
From the riyat emerging immediately after a believer's death (the higher riyat), the nasut-e-zilli of successors are formed.
The riyat emerging during the three days after burial form the nasut-e-tabii.
Purified riyat descend on uncooked fruits like apples; when the Imam and his wife eat these, conception of the Farzand-e-Imam follows.
Imam Jafar al-Sadiq told Mufaddal bin Umar that what the Imams eat is riyat, not external food.
The believer receives riyat during wudu, sahri (pre-dawn meal) and iftar (breaking fast); hence isbagh al-wudu is meritorious.
After wudu shake off water drops; an angel is created from each drop praying for forgiveness.
Reciting salawat and Surah al-Qadr (inna anzalna) after wudu makes prayer accepted.
Sahri should be eaten at the last moment; iftar should be hurried.
The Imam has three veils (tabii, zilli, khas), paralleling the three jewels of the shahadah (alif, lam, ha).
Every Imam from Hussain combined four ranks; Imam Hasan had two ranks (Imamate and succession) and Hussain had two lower.
The first Imam with whom the four ranks were truly combined was Ali Zayn al-Abidin, called Adam-e-Aal-e-Aba.
The Prophet's four ranks: the two higher Imamate ranks were kept as amanat with Abu Talib for Ali; mission and prophethood passed via Abd al-Muttalib.
Man kuntu mawlahu fa hadha Aliyyun mawlahu means the ranks Allah made me master of, Ali is now master.
The four ranks parallel the four sections of the shahadah (la, ilaha, illa, Allah).
The seventh Imam is the station of rest (istirahat al-maqam), being the jami (gatherer); paralleled by seven points where the pen lifts when writing the shahadah.
The twelve islands (jazair) house twelve noble qalban, paralleling the twelve letters in the great shahadah; the totals 2+3+4+7+12 make 28, the nizam al-alam al-ala.
True qalb haqiqi lies beneath the outer Baytullah which is its hijab; the outer Bayt is veil to the veiled inner heart.
Paradise (allati uiddat li-lladhina ahsanu al-husna wa ziyadah) is for those who took the ahd al-sharif and increased; their rank in the next karrah will surpass this one.
Amir al-Muminin said: al-hasanatu hubbuna wa-l-sayyiatu bughduna (the good deed is our love, the evil deed is hatred of us).
Whatever rank a believer dies in, it is incumbent on Allah's power to bring him to that rank again in the next karrah.
In the heart are three cavities (thalatha tajwifat), like the three jewels.
Sayyidna Hibatullah bin Ibrahim made a list of hudud ranking Sayyidna Mulla Karamullah Sahab at 28th, Ismail bin Hibatullah at 8th, Ali bin Hiba at 1st.
In the sakhrah beneath the Baytullah are ten abrar (righteous); Nimrud is the last because he claimed to be God.
The kalimat al-shahadah has come in five tones in the Quran; La ilaha illa anta occurs once (in Surah Yunus's supplication).
Muhammadun Rasulullah appears once in the Quran, in verse 29 of Surah al-Fath, indicating the Prophet was 29th in the sequence; Ali was 28th.
The 29th in any sequence breaks/enters into the sequence; Sayyidna Jafar is the 28th of the duat, and Muhammad bin Faraj the 29th.
A hujjah equals thirty duat; after Sayyidna Jafar all duat have been established in the rank of hujjah.
The Quran's letters classify into nurani-khafifah, nurani-thaqilah, zulmani-khafifah, zulmani-thaqilah; the muqattaat use no zulmani letters.
Imam Jafar al-Sadiq used Kaf-Ha-Ya-Ayn-Sad as a wasilah in his daily supplications.
The 29 muqattaat form, from the non-repeated ones, the single sentence Siratu Aliyyin haqq numsikuhu (Ali's path is truth, we hold to it).
With Imam Jafar al-Sadiq there were two states: outward Shia and batini Shia who were gradually advancing through his silence.
The Rukn al-Asad (Most Fortunate Corner of the Bayt) is formed from the fudulat of Amir al-Muminin in the first kawr cycles.
Fudulat here means purified riyat that have progressed, not bodily remnants; they are divided in five parts and one-fifth reaches hudud al-dawah.
Holy stones like aqiq (carnelian) and yaqut (ruby) are formed from fudulat of the Duat Kiram.
The Imam's nasut khas conception happens in the Bayt al-Haram; the Quranic ayat waj-alna li-l-muttaqin imama was rebuked by the Imam to one who recited it during tawaf.
The Prophet declared ana ibn al-karrat wa mumtahin al-awqat: I am son of the recurring cycles and tried by the times.
Allah tested the Prophet seven times before risalat and seven after; similarly Ali was tested fourteen times.
Sayyidna Yusuf bin Sulayman was tested by Sayyidna Muhammad Husayn for forty days, being sent away each morning before being embraced.
Mawlana al-Sadiq said: we were in the past cycles in our persons and our representatives.
Imam Jafar al-Sadiq said Aristotle (Aba Muhammad Aristatalis) was from us Ahl al-Bayt, as was Salman al-Farsi.
Salman al-Farsi is the only person in the Dawr al-Sitr who became Bab al-Abwab for both the Nabi and the Wasi.
The angels glorified Ali (sabbahatuhu al-malaikah al-qudsaniyyah) yearning for his vision; Allah created his likeness in the heavens which they glorify night and day.
The Quranic fi-l-samai ilahun wa fi-l-ardi ilah refers to Ali's likeness in heaven and Ali's presence on earth.
Harun (who died before Musa) is the meaning of one who is transferred in his lifetime; Ali is to the Prophet as Harun was to Musa.
The nur al-azim Ali passed away in the Prophet's lifetime, with awsiya passing before their anbiya in inner reality.
The Mim took the successorship of the Ayn (Ali was veiled by the Mim of Maryamah); the Mim was established by the veil of the Ayn on Ghadir.
The muhtajib of Ali (named Ayn) is superior (afdal) to the muhtajib of the Prophet; but the hijab of the Prophet is superior to the hijab of Ali.
Three sufara (envoys) of the Rasul: Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib (with Abdullah), and Ali/Rasul; this is a conjunction (qiran) sequence.
Ali is al-awwal wa-l-akhir; he gathered the past Imams (Hunayd to Hakim) and gathered those who would come (Hasan to the Qaim).
Imam Jafar al-Sadiq manifested his ghaybah through his son Ismail's death, then said to Furat bin Ahmad: anta ana wa ana anta (you are me and I am you).
When the Imam recited Surah al-Muddaththir on Furat, his external garb changed and people greeted him as Imam al-Zaman.
In Sayyidna Dawud bin Ajabshah's time, Lad bin Dhannu of Ahmedabad (an Agha Khani horse merchant) embraced Dawudi rite and became dai of Jazira of Sindh.
The seven great intellects each give material support to a paralleling natiq in the rank order (third intellect supports Adam, fourth supports Nuh, etc.).
The fifth intellect in this meaning is al-Husayn ibn Ali, fifth from the Prophet in the Panjatan-i Pak.
The qudar al-Fatimiyyah (Fatimi powers) are the Aimmah from Husayn's progeny, called Fatimi because of awe before Fatimah al-Zahra's station.
Sayyidna Ibrahim bin Muhammad al-Fad wrote Kanz al-Ulum which clarifies that the Aimmah after Husayn are called Aimmah Fatimiyyin.
Sayyidna Ibrahim bin Husayn al-Hamidi wrote Kanz al-Walad for his son Sayyidna Hatim.
Al-hamd has numerical value 52 (ha 8 + mim 40 + dal 4), referring to three (Muhammad/Ali/Fatimah) plus 49 Imams up to Abu al-Aimmah.
Wabud rabbaka hatta yatiyaka al-yaqin: yaqin means death and also Amir al-Muminin who will question you after death.
The Prophet said the essence of iman is walayah and love for Ali, not prayer/fasting/Hajj/jihad.
In raja (return), each returns in the same rank as he died: Bab as Bab, Hujjah as Hujjah, Dai as Dai, Madhun as Madhun, Mukasir as Mukasir, mumin as mumin.
Those who die in childhood without taking ahd al-sharif will be born in the state of iman in future karrahs.
In raja, one is born in the same place: minha khalaqnakum wa fiha nuiidukum wa minha nukhrijukum.
The two prostrations in prayer correspond to khalaqnakum (creation) and nuiidukum (return).
The 1000-year period of return is fixed for both mumin and non-mumin.
On the 21st of any month, inauspiciousness (nahusat) gathers; Imam Jafar al-Sadiq composed a rare insistent dua for this date.
The 21st is also the day of passing of the awsiya.
Common Ayat al-Kursi mistakes: al-Aliyyu al-Azim should be al-Aliyya al-Azim (with zabar) at the end.
Seven istighfars at end of Ayat al-Kursi correspond to seven dawr al-sitr cycles, ours being the seventh manifestation.
Inna hadha siratu Aliyyin mustaqim (Quranic): the path of Ali is straight.
Opponents of Aimmah and followers are gathered in dhanab (Ketu/tail); opponents of Anbiya and Duat in ras (Rahu/head).
Souls of opponents of Aimmah/Anbiya are thrown by divine providence to inauspicious peripheral places, made into animal/mountain forms with senses intact for torment.
In the slaughter (dhabihah) saying Allahu Akbar separates the nafs al-hissiyyah from the animal, making its meat halal.
After cooking meat, allow steam to escape; the remaining nafs al-hissiyyah departs through the steam.
In states of punishment they neither live nor die (la yahya wa la yamut); killed and revived a thousand times daily.
The form of every believer gathers at the Bab al-Abwab (called bahr al-zakhar, fasl al-khitab); the Imam grants this gathering to his son who becomes Imam bil-fil.
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-Aliyy al-Azim: Aliyy al-Azim is the ayn al-aimmah (essence of Imams), all Aimmah are hijabs of Aliyy al-Azim.
The ghayah (ultimate) of stones/minerals is the ruby (yaqut); the ghayah of animals is the elephant (for its intelligence); the ghayah of man is the mumin (believer).
Awwalu man amana has the numerical value of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
On the night of Miraj two things were bestowed unique to the Prophet: Surat al-Fatiha and the last two verses of Surah al-Baqarah.
Falak al-Muhit alone of all entities ascends directly without touching the earth, becoming the Universal Intellect.
At kawr's end the aflak and kawakib descend; jewels and rubies take their khilafat in service for one kawr of Adam.
Sayyidna Abdullah ibn Thamir was a mubashshir al-nabi who gave glad tidings of the Prophet's coming; he died at Ukhdud, Najran (mentioned in Surah Buruj).
Visitation of graves is a connection to the rank above for intercession at the gathering of forms (majami al-suwar).
Hudud al-dawah were angels bil-quwwah in life and become angels bil-fil after death.
The Prophet said parents feel joy when children visit their graves, as they did when children sat in their laps.
Wabtaghu ilayhi al-wasilah means reach Allah through Rasul, Ahl al-Bayt, or duat/hujjat/imam, not through the Quran.
Marifat of the Worshipped is marifat of the hudud; the gnosis of Allah is inside the gnosis of the hudud.
Surah al-Fatihah has 7 verses and 25 words; the 25 words equal 25 Quranic prophets and correspond to 12 duat of jazair + 12 duat of hadarat + the Imam.
Duat of jazair pair (hence tahajjud's pairs); duat of hadarat are collective (hence salat al-layl's 12 consecutive rakat).
The dhibh al-hadi in Mina elevates the meat to the upright lineage; its hissiyya is punished and expelled by Bismillah being uttered.
Slaughter by Jews and Christians using their own language is halal (jaiz).
Prayer is the sacrifice of every pious person (as-salatu qurbanu kulli taqiyyin); the believer says Allahu Akbar over himself.
Best four-phrase litany per the Prophet: Subhanallah, walhamdulillah, wa la ilaha illallah, wallahu akbar, plus la hawla wa la quwwata.
Allahu Akbar acts on namiyah, Alhamdulillah on hissiyah, Subhanallah on natiqah; La ilaha illallah is the form upon the nayyirah.
The natiqa absorbs the hissiya throughout life and at death; the hissiya remaining in the body is a bad death; absorbed into the natiqa is noble.
Ali bin Sulayman said if pre-eternity had not decided I would precede Ibrahim, I never could have preceded him.
Ali bin Sulayman performed 11 nusus on Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Fahd during his 14-year imprisonment by the Zaidi Imam.
Azdad of awliya Allah are given 40 days respite to roam between heavens and earth harming believers, then pulled into Ras al-Zanab.
From fuzala of hudud al-dawah three things form: jewels in royal crowns, pigeons of Baytullah/Madinah (whose own death is halal), and the salt used at meals.
Umar bin Abd al-Aziz returned Bagh-e-Fadak to Ahl al-Bayt and stopped cursing of Ali from 70,000 pulpits; for this his punishment was shortened.

At the Qiyamah of the Qayam, opposers (Yazid, Muawiyah, Marwan, Nimrud, Firaun) will be dragged in human form to Mina, killed by believers; stench will be carried by wind through four doors of safrah (one in Hadramaut).
Mawla Bibi Fatimah corresponds to Muzdalifah; Mawla Ali to Mina; Rasulullah to Jabal Arafat; these three are the lubab of the Dawr al-Satr.
On Yawm Arafah the camel of the Prophet would sit down under the weight of descending revelation.
On Jabal Arafat luminous suwarat manifest never occurring to a human heart, intensified by what was unfolding regarding Ghadir Khumm.
Aisha told her father Abu Bakr the Prophet's secret about Ali's succession; this led to munafiqin planning to kill the Prophet in a dark valley.
At the dark valley before Ghadir, lightning flashed prolonged so the Prophet and Hudhayfah al-Yamani saw the would-be killers' faces.
Cutting trees in Arafat is forbidden because they neighbor the hidden khamair (treasures).
Whoever broadcasts the secrets of the dawah has prepared his seat in fire and is disavowed by al-Aziz al-Ghaffar.
Dawud bin Ajabshah's first nass on Sulayman bin Hasan was long, written by Dawud bin Qutb, using 28 titles corresponding to the 28 letters of the kalimat al-shahadah.
Sayyidna Muhammad bin Fad al-Alawi established that after this nass anyone reciting the kalimah must also bear shahadah for Sulayman bin Hasan.
Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan was at maqam-e-nasut for his Imam and at maqam-e-lahut for his fellow believers.
The Dai of Yemen is superior to all duat of other islands and does not lead prayer outside the three jazair (Yemen, Hind, Sindh).
The mansub of Yemen (Najran) is superior to all manasib because he is the dai's successor bil-quwwah.
When ifadah and istifadah occur, souls of deceased believers attend; the questioner asks through the tongue of a hadd-i ali.
Sayyidi Fardali Sahib Muqaddas sent a possessed Bohra woman to Ziyali Sahib Muqaddas to instruct him to conduct asbaq in the mosque so departed suwarat could hear.
There are two Mehdis: the 11th Imam Mehdi, and the 50th Imam Mehdi (Mehdi Akhir al-Zaman) who is outside the circle of Imamate, the Mim al-Akhirah.
Sayyidna Husayn bin Ismail taught al-Mehdi huwal Qaim wal Qaim huwal Mehdi.
Mehdi is the Qaim of dawr al-sitr; he is the confluence of eight surahs corresponding to the eight angels carrying Allah's throne.
The Qaim takes the khilafah of the Ashir upon departure from this abode and remains qaim for only three days.
Sirat mustaqim refers to the line of juz-i duat in which one stands; the believer's sirat mustaqim is the chain from believer to Imam through lower and higher hudud to the Bab al-Abwab.
Spiritual progress is of two types: one striven for, the other obtained by sitting in someone's lap.
In a kawr there are 360 manifestations of the walad's integration; the human body contains 360 nufus, of which one part progresses per kawr.
In Surah Yasin the Quranic ana ala siratin mustaqim refers to Abu Talib (my Lord) being on the straight path of juzs.
The rolling-up of the heaven (yawma natwi al-samaa) occurs at the end of the kawr when the ribatat (bonds) terminate.
After each end-of-kawr, the earth is changed, length becomes width, north becomes south; kama badana awwala khalqin nuiduhu applies.
Dawr al-sitr and dawr al-kashf succeed each other like night and day until the Mawr al-Azam is completed.
One mawr contains 400,000 kawr times 400,000 kawr; one mawr has passed and nine remain.
At each end-of-mawr the Ashir's place is taken by the ninth aql; all ascending forms gather in the domain of the Mumbaith al-Awwal.
In the end, all are absorbed into the Mumbaith al-Awwal; only the domain of the Aql al-Awwal and Mumbaith al-Awwal remain.
Risalah by Nasir al-Din al-Tusi excoriates Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Muawiyah, and Yazid with severe titles in a 15-20 page treatise.
In the cave (Surah al-Tawbah), tranquility descended on the Prophet only, not on Abu Bakr; Shahriyar the dai proved Abu Bakr was outside the circle of faith.
After Saqifah Bani Saidah the body of the Prophet was left unburied while Abu Bakr's allegiance was extracted at swordpoint by Umar.
Confidants of the era of Isa (six individuals) gathered the precious treasures of Isa's teachings and joined the Prophet's circle.
Hudhayfah al-Yamani witnessed the cave conspiracy with the Prophet and confirmed to Umar by oath he was among the conspirators.
The Prophet during his final illness repeatedly asked whether Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman had joined Usamah's expedition (they refused).
Imam Jafar al-Sadiq taught that in the previous cycles we existed both in our persons and in our representatives.
The dawah is presented to non-believers at the time of every death and when they change bodies (qalib), until they reach the garment of tar (damar) where it is no longer offered.
Holy graves remain blessed by their athar even after fuzala have progressed, like fragrance lingering in an empty perfume bottle.
If the visitor at a grave is of higher rank than the buried, the flow of aids reverses, descending from visitor to buried.
The Bismillahilladhi la yadurru maa ismihi shayun fil-ardi wa la fis-samai dua recited three times morning and evening protects the reciter from all harm.
Eid al-Adha meat and aqiqah meat must not be given to non-Muslims; a nursing mother must not eat or drink from her child's aqiqah lest the child's milk become unlawful for him.
Wild animals dying their own death remain in a fallen state until raja; the pigeons of Baytullah and Madinah are excepted, their natural death being halal.
At end of one kawr, lava-released souls who had done some good deeds emerge before completion of qawr-e-azam through volcanoes, becoming soil, vegetation, and food for further refinement.
Today's Imam Abul Qaim's Mehdi (the 50th) and the Qaim are two different personalities, but the Qaim of dawr al-sitr was called Mehdi.
Sayyidna Sulayman ibn Hasan was given title Amin al-Mutaman by Sayyidna Dawud ibn Ajabshah.
Today's Imam (35th) is seventh of his haftah and combines two haftahs, possessing 14 Imams; his Dai's station rises with him.
The Prophet was the 29th in the Imam-line counting from Janab Ibrahim through the appointed Imams.
In their lifetime hudud receive part of the Imam's mawad temporarily, returning it on their passing.
Allah's favor of forming the soul from the body must not be reversed by inserting soul back into body; doing so is shirk zulmun azim.
Sayyidi Raj wrote down the second nass of Dawud bin Ajabshah on Sulayman bin Hasan three days before his passing in 970 Hijri.
At Ali bin Sulayman's majlis Sayyidna Sulayman bin Hasan would visit invisibly; Ali would stand and greet him.
Sayyidna Husayn bin Ismail at Tawaf saw the souls of Fardali, Ziyali, and Ghulam Husayn doing tawaf at high speed, prompting him to cry Wa shauqah.
Husayn bin Ismail in Najran kissed the hand of a sudden visitor who vanished; believed to have been Imam Ali himself.
Sulayman bin Hasan (in his island form) also had a form in Hadramawt named Humam (Sulayman-i Humam) unprecedented among others.
Sayyidna Husayn bin Ahmad was under house arrest in Taif and would come to Baytullah performing seven tawaf daily.
